findings.claim: `self.downsize` is defined twice in OptimizedImage. Ruby has no overloading, so the later (from, to, dimensions, opts) definition replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) one, and existing 5-argument callers such as ResizeEmoji (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) raise ArgumentError.

verifier.reason: In app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151, self.downsize is defined twice, so the second 3..4-argument definition at app/models/optimized_image.rb:149-151 overwrites the 4..5-argument definition at app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-147. Consequently, the 5-argument call OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts) in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 raises ArgumentError.

findings.claim: The same 10 MB constant is duplicated in several places, so the client and server limits can drift apart.

verifier.reason: The 10 MB upload limit is hardcoded in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 and app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 (`10 * 1024`), as well as on the server in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 (`10.megabytes`) and config/nginx.sample.conf:61 (`client_max_body_size 10m`). Because these hardcoded values are duplicated rather than derived from a shared setting or constant, the client and server limits can drift apart.
